Editorial interior photograph of a real, lived-in home in Mexico City, upper-middle-class (colonia like Coyoacán, Roma or Del Valle), photographed by an architectural interiors photographer for a paint brand's inspiration magazine. Full-frame camera, 28 mm lens, camera height 1.2 m, verticals perfectly corrected, deep depth of field (f/8). Natural late-afternoon window light entering from the left side, warm and soft, casting gentle shadows of window mullions and leaves across part of the painted wall; the shadows cover less than one third of the wall. True-to-life color, natural white balance slightly warm, no color grading look, realistic dynamic range with detail in the shadows, very subtle film grain. Real materials with honest imperfections: solid wood grain, slightly creased linen, hand-thrown ceramics, worn handwoven wool rug, a few objects slightly out of place. Restrained, uncluttered styling with one or two discreet Mexican craft objects (black barro jar, small talavera piece, palm-leaf basket, agave in a clay pot). The painted wall is the protagonist: a flat matte painted surface, smooth, evenly painted, occupying 40 to 55 percent of the frame, seen frontally; its color must read clearly and accurately. Keep the upper third of the painted wall completely clear of frames, shelves or objects (empty wall space for later labels), keep generous wall above the furniture, and keep the lower-left corner of the frame calm (floor or rug, no important objects). Nothing important within 12 percent of the left and right edges. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, signage, logos, brand names, paint cans, posters with writing or book titles anywhere. No people, no pets. It must look like a real photograph of a real home, not a 3D render, not CGI, not an AI image: avoid plastic surfaces, avoid perfect symmetry, avoid overly glossy floors, avoid generic American suburban interiors, avoid the cliché of a bouclé sofa with a round coffee table, olive tree and arch prints.

Space: living room with a dining nook visible at the right. Main wall, facing the camera, painted Berel "Calor de Hogar" 321N, a warm terracotta, exact paint color hex #AA5F3F (sRGB 170,95,63) as seen under neutral daylight. A short side wall or passage at the right is painted Berel "Canela Mascabado" 1-1209D, a soft cinnamon beige, exact hex #B69771. Furniture: low sofa upholstered in oatmeal linen with a folded striped Mexican wool throw, a pair of leather-and-wood armchairs, rectangular parota wood coffee table, large indoor plant (not an olive tree) in a terracotta pot, floor lamp with a linen shade, terrazzo floor with a handwoven rug. Wall above the sofa left bare.
